code: set.seed(1) n_geno <- 120 n_env  <- 4 lines  <- paste0("L", seq_len(n_geno)) envs   <- paste0("E", seq_len(n_env))  # Genomic relationship matrix M  <- matrix(rnorm(n_geno^2), n_geno) G0 <- tcrossprod(M) / n_geno diag(G0) <- diag(G0) + 0.5 dimnames(G0) <- list(lines, lines)  # Broad TPE: environments with a mix of positive and negative genetic # correlations (this is what makes connectivity matter). Sigma_E <- matrix(c( 1.0,  0.6,  0.2, -0.1,                      0.6,  1.0,  0.3,  0.0,                      0.2,  0.3,  1.0,  0.5,                     -0.1,  0.0,  0.5,  1.0), 4, 4) dimnames(Sigma_E) <- list(envs, envs)  # Fully balanced positive control: every line in every environment. alloc_full <- matrix(1L, n_geno, n_env, dimnames = list(lines, envs))  # Random sparse allocation, each line in ~2 of 4 environments. alloc_sparse <- allocate_sparse_met(   treatments                     = lines,   environments                   = envs,   allocation_method              = "random_balanced",   n_test_entries_per_environment = 60,   target_replications            = 2,   allow_approximate              = TRUE,   seed                           = 1 )$allocation_matrix  # Equireplicate allocation with correlation-adaptive distinct-treatment # connectivity. Maximin protects the weakest target-attainment pair. alloc_eqr <- allocate_sparse_met(   treatments                     = lines,   environments                   = envs,   allocation_method              = "equireplicate",   n_test_entries_per_environment = 60,   target_replications            = 2,   Sigma_E                        = Sigma_E,   pair_aggregate                 = "maximin",   seed                           = 1 )$allocation_matrix  # Refine the equireplicate allocation directly against the coupled G x E # objective (minimise across-TPE PEV). alloc_opt <- optimize_allocation_gxe(   alloc_eqr, G = G0, Sigma_E = Sigma_E, iter = 100, seed = 1 )$allocation_matrix  # Design-based coupled PEV / CDmean (lower PEV, higher CDmean is better). sapply(list(full = alloc_full, sparse = alloc_sparse,             equireplicate = alloc_eqr, optimised = alloc_opt),        function(A) met_information(A, G = G0, Sigma_E = Sigma_E)$mean_PEV)  # Realised selection accuracy and genetic gain across the TPE. sapply(list(full = alloc_full, sparse = alloc_sparse,             equireplicate = alloc_eqr, optimised = alloc_opt),        function(A) simulate_met(A, G = G0, Sigma_E = Sigma_E,                                 n_sim = 50, seed = 1)$accuracy_mean)

title: End-to-End Sparse MET Pipeline: from Environmental Classification to the Combined Field Book
text: OptiSparseMET designs sparse multi-environment trials (METs) optimising two coupled levels : Level 1 — across-environment allocation: genotypes tested environments, whole network genetically connected every line predictable across target population environments (TPE). Level 2 — within-environment field layout: site laid (blocks, checks, alpha row-column), sets precisely plot measured. tutorial runs entire pipeline end end, organised module, realistic--simulated rice testcross program: Module 1 — Environmental classification (enviromics). Build environment kernels weather / soil / management / geography, calibrate data-driven environmental covariance ΣE\Sigma_E, cluster sites mega-environments. Module 2 — Genetic relationship matrices. Genomic G (VanRaden), hybrid/testcross GRM optional dominance, made-invertible tune-. Module 3 — Sparse allocation. Feasibility, auto-suggested common treatments, M3 / M4 allocation per-site capacities. Module 4 — Seed-aware replication. Turn single seed inventory feasible replication plan (p-rep / augmented). Module 5 — Within-environment field design. Block-based repeated-check designs alpha row-column designs, efficiency evaluation. Module 6 — Coupled optimisation & information. two-level information matrix, exact multi-trait index reliability, criterion + gain + cost objectives, exchange/SA optimisation, Pareto frontier. Module 7 — Simulation. Monte-Carlo prediction accuracy realised gain. Module 8 — Benchmarking. Complete / random / M3 / M4 / optimised designs compared confidence intervals, decision stability, tail risk. Module 9 — Field books & field maps. Per-site combined field books, field map drawn layout. one-call wrapper (plan_sparse_met_design()) validation appendix close vignette.

title: Multi-trait index weights from desired genetic gains — desired_gain_weights
text: Two sources supported: "pesek_baker" (default, built-) classical desired-gain index Pesek & Baker (1969): genetic (co)variance matrix \(G\) signed desired gains \(d\), weights \(b = G^{-1} d\). expected genetic gains index selection proportional \(G b\), makes realised gains proportional \(d\) exactly. Deterministic dependency-free. "dgqgsi" Extracts optimised index-weight vector result produced DGQGSI package (Akohoue 2026; run_desired_gain_index_Joukhadar2024() / run_dgsi_qgsi_pipeline()), optimises desired-gain indices (quadratic genomic variant) breeding data. Pass result dgqgsi_result; weight vector stored non-standard name, give weights_field. Desired gains supplied positive magnitudes; traits named lower_is_better sign flipped internally (convention DGQGSI), smaller value counts gain.

title: Multi-trait index weights from desired genetic gains — desired_gain_weights

text: features computed phenological time – series indexed day--start, sites different season lengths compared common footing (dynamic time warping used: warping erase timing signal want keep). Windows / stages windows may single integer K (split season K equal intervals – crop knowledge needed), numeric vector day--start cut points (e.g. c(30, 60, 90)), named list day ranges crop physiology (e.g. list(vegetative = c(0, 40), flowering = c(40, 70), grain_fill = c(70, 120))). Expert stages give interpretable features; equal intervals thermal-time cut points knowledge-free alternatives. Statistics stats (e.g. "mean", "sd", "cv", "sum", "min", "max", "median") computed per window per parameter; "sd" "cv" capture day--day variability mean hides. Stress days thresholds counts days meeting condition per window, e.g. list(heat_days = list(par = "T2M_MAX", = 35)). Growing degree days gdd accumulates degree days per window, e.g. list(gdd = list(par = "T2M", base = 10, upper = 30)). Functional functional fits B-spline basis normalised season time returns coefficients shape features, e.g. list(temp_shape = list(par = "T2M", df = 4)).

Default 1. prop Selected proportion. Default 0.1. trait_weights Optional index weights multi-trait target, typically desired_gain_weights() (desired gains, economic weights). trait_gencov Optional trait genetic (co)variance matrix (length(trait_weights) square) index; NULL identity used.

text: list gain (\(\Delta G\) \(\Delta H\)), intensity, accuracy (\(r\)), sigma (target SD used).

title: Expected genetic gain of a design — expected_genetic_gain
text: Single trait. \(\sigma = \sqrt{\sigma_g^2}\) \(\Delta G = \sqrt{r^2}\,\sigma_g\). Note one trait \(\Delta G\) monotone transform reliability, maximising gain maximising CDmean equivalent objectives; gain scale becomes distinct multi-trait case comparing targets different \(\sigma_g\). Multi-trait index. index weights \(w\) genetic (co)variance matrix among traits \(\Sigma_T\), aggregate genotype \(H = w'g\) standard deviation \(\sigma_I = \sqrt{w'\Sigma_T w}\), \(\Delta H = \,r\,\sigma_I\). Rather subjective economic weights, recommended way obtain \(w\) breeder-defined desired gains via desired_gain_weights() (classical Pesek-Baker, DGQGSI package). uses design's reliability index assumes traits share design (measured plots) – first-order approximation, full multi-trait mixed-model PEV.

text: -criterion (lower = better): $$A_\text{criterion} = \bar{v}_\text{diff} =   \frac{2}{p(p-1)} \sum_{<j} \text{Var}(\hat{\tau}_i - \hat{\tau}_j)$$ D-criterion (lower = better): $$D_\text{criterion} = \exp\!\left(\frac{\log\det(HVH)}{p-1}\right)$$ \(H = I_p - p^{-1}J_p\) centring matrix \(V\) treatment variance-covariance submatrix. Efficiency forms (higher = better): $$A_\text{efficiency} = 1 / A_\text{criterion}, \quad       D_\text{efficiency} = 1 / D_\text{criterion}$$

title: Evaluate the statistical efficiency of an alpha-lattice design — met_evaluate_alpha_efficiency
text: PEV-criterion (lower = better): mean prediction error variance across entry lines. $$\text{PEV}_\text{criterion} = \frac{1}{p}\sum_{=1}^{p}   \text{Var}(\hat{u}_i - u_i)$$ CDmean (higher = better): mean coefficient determination genomic breeding value prediction (Rincent et al. 2012, Genetics 192:715-728). $$\text{CDmean} = 1 - \frac{\text{PEV}_\text{criterion}}{\sigma_g^2}$$ CDmean measures proportion genetic variance explained GEBV predictions average across lines. Values close 1 indicate highly reliable predictions; values close 0 indicate near-uninformative predictions. CDmean defined treatment_effect = "random". CD per line: number treatments exceed eff_full_max, per-line coefficient determination vector also returned: $$CD_i = 1 - \text{PEV}_i / \sigma_g^2$$

text: G x E effects \(u\) (one per line--environment cell) prior covariance \(\sigma_g^2\,(\Sigma_E \otimes G)\), prior precision \(\sigma_g^{-2}(\Sigma_E^{-1} \otimes G^{-1})\). present cell \((j,e)\) contributes diagonal information \(d_{je} = \text{reps}_{je}\, \epsilon_e / \sigma_e^2\), \(\epsilon_e \(0,1]\) within-environment efficiency factor (local design's / CDmean evaluation). Environment means absorbed fixed effects, giving effect information matrix $$C_{uu} = D - D X (X^\top D X)^{-1} X^\top D + \sigma_g^{-2}   (\Sigma_E^{-1} \otimes G^{-1}).$$ (absorption form verified match full mixed-model-equations solution.) across-TPE breeding value line \(j\) \(\bar u_j = E^{-1}\sum_e u_{je}\); PEV \(a_j^\top C_{uu}^{-1} a_j\) \(a_j\) averaging line \(j\)'s cells, reliability \(\text{CD}_j = 1 - \text{PEV}_j / \operatorname{Var}(\bar u_j)\).

text: met_prep_famoptg() OptiSparseMET version prep_famoptg() OptiDesign package. met_ prefix avoids namespace conflicts packages loaded simultaneously. arguments, return values, internal logic identical prep_famoptg() OptiDesign. met_prep_famoptg() builds repeated-check block design plant breeding agronomic experiments. Check treatments included every block, non-check treatments allocated according user-specified replication levels. Depending treatment structure supplied, function generates three design classes: Augmented repeated-check design: checks repeated every block, test entries unreplicated (p_rep_treatments = NULL). Partially replicated (p-rep) repeated-check design: mixture replicated unreplicated non-check entries. RCBD-type repeated-check design: non-check entries given replication across blocks. Design evaluation separated construction. function returns field book, layout matrix, seed . compute , D, CDmean optimality criteria call met_evaluate_famoptg_efficiency() returned field_book. search optimised design across many randomisations call met_optimize_famoptg().

text: Let: \(c\) = number check treatments \(b\) = n_blocks \(v_p\) = number p-rep treatments replication counts \(r_1, r_2, \ldots, r_{v_p}\) \(v_u\) = number unreplicated treatments Total plots required: $$\text{total} = b \times c + \sum_{=1}^{v_p} r_i + v_u$$ Allocation rules enforced construction: Checks Appear every block. check contributes \(b\) plots total. P-rep treatments treatment \(\) appears exactly \(r_i\) blocks, always distinct blocks - never twice block. core p-rep constraint. Unreplicated treatments Appear exactly full design, distributed evenly possible across blocks.

RCBD-type repeated-check design - obtained non-check treatments supplied via p_rep_treatments common replication count greater 1. count equals n_blocks, every non-check treatment appears every block - closest repeated-check analogue classical RCBD.

title: Compute the minimum per-environment capacity for full treatment coverage — min_k_for_full_coverage
text: Let \(J\) total number treatments, \(C\) number common treatments assigned every environment, \(\) number environments. number sparse (non-common) treatments : $$J^* = J - C$$ Common treatments consume \(C\) slots every environment sparse allocation begins. number sparse-allocatable slots per environment : $$k_e^* = k_e - C$$ every sparse treatment appear least one environment, total number sparse slots across environments must satisfy: $$\sum_{e=1}^{} k_e^* \geq J^*$$ equal per-environment capacity, minimum number sparse slots per environment : $$k^*_{\min} = \left\lceil J^* / \right\rceil$$ corresponding minimum total entries per environment : $$k_{\min} = k^*_{\min} + C$$ function returns quantities. value min_total_entries_per_environment passed n_test_entries_per_environment guarantee full coverage minimum capacity.

title: Construct a repeated-check block design with flexible replication structure — prep_famoptg
code: data("OptiSparseMET_example_data", package = "OptiSparseMET") x <- OptiSparseMET_example_data  env_trt <- x$treatments[1:24] env_fam <- x$treatment_info$Family[match(env_trt, x$treatment_info$Treatment)]  ## Example 1: p-rep repeated-check design — first 8 entries replicated ## twice, remaining 16 unreplicated. Checks in every block. out_prep <- prep_famoptg(   check_treatments         = c("CHK1", "CHK2"),   check_families           = c("CHECK", "CHECK"),   p_rep_treatments         = env_trt[1:8],   p_rep_reps               = rep(2L, 8),   p_rep_families           = env_fam[1:8],   unreplicated_treatments  = env_trt[9:24],   unreplicated_families    = env_fam[9:24],   n_blocks                 = 4,   n_rows                   = 6,   n_cols                   = 8,   order                    = "row",   serpentine               = TRUE,   seed                     = 123,   cluster_source           = "Family",   eval_efficiency          = FALSE,   use_dispersion           = FALSE ) #> Warning: Field size (6 x 8 = 48) does not match required (40). Adjusting dimensions.  dim(out_prep$layout_matrix)   # 6 x 8 #> [1] 6 7 head(out_prep$field_book) #>        Treatment Family Gcluster Block Plot Row Column #> plot_1      L008    F06     <NA>     1    1   1      1 #> plot_2      L012    F14     <NA>     1    2   1      2 #> plot_3      CHK2  CHECK     <NA>     1    3   1      3 #> plot_4      L015    F10     <NA>     1    4   1      4 #> plot_5      L002    F15     <NA>     1    5   1      5 #> plot_6      L007    F02     <NA>     1    6   1      6 out_prep$seed_used #> [1] 123  if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{ ## Example 2: augmented repeated-check design — no replicated entries, ## all 24 test entries unreplicated. out_aug <- prep_famoptg(   check_treatments         = c("CHK1", "CHK2"),   check_families           = c("CHECK", "CHECK"),   p_rep_treatments         = character(0),   p_rep_reps               = integer(0),   p_rep_families           = character(0),   unreplicated_treatments  = env_trt,   unreplicated_families    = env_fam,   n_blocks                 = 4,   n_rows                   = 5,   n_cols                   = 6,   order                    = "row",   serpentine               = FALSE,   seed                     = 123,   cluster_source           = "Family",   eval_efficiency          = FALSE,   use_dispersion           = FALSE )  dim(out_aug$layout_matrix) head(out_aug$field_book)  ## Example 3: RCBD-type repeated-check design — all 24 entries replicated ## 4 times (once per block). Equivalent to a classical RCBD with repeated ## checks. out_rcbd <- prep_famoptg(   check_treatments         = c("CHK1", "CHK2"),   check_families           = c("CHECK", "CHECK"),   p_rep_treatments         = env_trt,   p_rep_reps               = rep(4L, length(env_trt)),   p_rep_families           = env_fam,   unreplicated_treatments  = character(0),   unreplicated_families    = character(0),   n_blocks                 = 4,   n_rows                   = 14,   n_cols                   = 8,   order                    = "row",   serpentine               = TRUE,   seed                     = 123,   cluster_source           = "Family",   eval_efficiency          = FALSE,   use_dispersion           = FALSE )  dim(out_rcbd$layout_matrix) head(out_rcbd$field_book) } # }
